creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Observed with Muster 0.24.0 on 2026-11-09. When a window socket accepts a connection but does not answer, `muster window --json` falls back to the local daemon and exits successfully. Its stdout contains two JSON documents: a one-line diagnostic object with a `note` field, followed by the actual window/daemon result.

A caller decoding stdout as one JSON value fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON`. The caller must detect and discard the diagnostic record before reading the result, although the documented non-watch JSON shape is a single result object.

Reproduce by running `muster window --json` while the window host is unreachable but its socket still accepts connections, then parse the complete stdout as one JSON document. The fallback itself works; the extra document breaks consumers.

Possibly: send the diagnostic to stderr, or include it in the result object, and exercise the fallback with a single-document JSON parser in a CLI contract test.
title: muster window --json fallback emits two JSON documents
